title: Exegesis of Proverbs and the Soul
english: to overwhelm

He speaks of things that are, and perceiving the precision of matters, such as the flint of God's judgments, he says these are clouds, or he calls the prophets clouds, chilling the teaching. Let it not be outside of the water of life which is profitable.

He speaks of 'will' as the movement concerning practical things; 'understanding' as that concerning theoretical things; 'neck' he says of the same soul, which bore the yoke of the Lord (Matt 11:29-30). Just as the neck encircles the breast-bands, so the soul carries the things of God in the kingdom, just as it does his commandments here. For the ungodly, even the prosperous things are cursed; but for the righteous, even the most humble things are blessed. He calls the powers of the rational soul a 'house'; and 'dwellings' the powers of the spirited and the appetitive; for within them the irrational suffer passions.

St. 7. The honor of wisdom is the keeping of the commandments; but wisdom is Christ, whose bride is the soul honoring him through virtues, which shall be received by him. St. 10. Just as a certain infant always sets forth struggles with attentions, and wakes him up when he is wandering off. And the springs of life are the virtues, from which the living water is (John 4:14), namely the knowledge of Christ. To the one progressing according to wisdom, many springs become, and not only one; but according to the abundance of virtues. To those who guard these exhortations, he says, they become life; these are the contest.

St. 13. Walk correctly in the course according to life, he says. The impulses of this soul are its feet; for virtue is a mean. St. 2. Do not attend to a deceptive teaching, enticed through flattering speech, that is, heresy, and idolatry, and vain words. St. 3. Until the hearing, their beauty. For such is the deception: the destructive is accustomed to hide, but the pleasant is set forth so as to be seen; otherwise they would have fled immediately. But God is not so; rather he hides the pleasant and sets forth the bitter. And he did not say, 'Flow away,' but, 'Recede,' so as not to encounter the bitterness, though later it is more bitter than bile; not so much the pleasant as the bitter, but much more.

St. 7. He says here the way for the mind leading to virtue (Prov 3:6); or perhaps virtue stands before us to separate us from evil. St. 11. That is, in old age; which, through the wearing out of the flesh, signifies incontinence.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Nature of Wisdom and Creation
english: Regarding some corruption. Prov 12, 14. He brings in the corrupted one, reproaching himself as one who hated instruction, and says: 'I would have perished even if I had not been corrupted, having wasted my flesh in dissipation, and having made this life small.' Therefore it became evident that my discipline was in the midst of the Church and the Synagogue. For the voice has repented, and not having occurred, it has become little by little. Similar is the saying, 'By little by little my waters were poured out' (Song 8:16). For having recovered and having perceived, he says: 'Where is the little by little?' How then can one console the madness which is from nature?

Prov 15. Knowledge is both a cistern and a fountain; to those coming to the virtues it is a cistern, but to those perfected by them, a fountain. And knowledge is called mother, and wife, and sister; mother, because through her we are born by the teacher; wife, because being joined it brings forth virtues and right doctrines; sister, because from one God we have become. And I called wisdom sister.
Prov 19, 17. See how it shows not only ease through abundance, but also having no one a partner in enjoyment; and it doubles itself and calls it possession; for one knows the pleasure of the matter.

Prov 6. Even if you imitate the natural work of the irrational: or be, that is, go forth. For many do good works from theory or hearing, and not from knowledge. A prophet and apostles say [it is like] bees, whose labors are useful to the great for their order and to the small; he says the matters are the wax, but the honey is the contemplation of these things. Just as the shepherd guides the goats, so the essence guides the bees. Therefore, in all things, order is good for life.
Prov 12. The fool is the atheist who has lost the theoretical, but the lawless one is he who has lost the practical.

Prov 1. Guard the common, so that it may be yours, he says, and to live an eternal life, and to become discerning. For the keeping of the divine commandments will shine for us much more brightly than the light of the eyes.
Prov 3. The hand is the whole action, but the finger is the more partial. Convinced, he says, you will have a wide heart for the reception of the virtues.
Prov 18. She makes it a point to dwell with a man, as if living according to law; and she rejects all things fearful and hindering, proposing a departure from the one dwelling with her.
Prov 27. For the house...

The ways of Hades, leading down into the chambers of death. For those who are persuaded by it, becoming earthly and mortal through it, thus they shall perish. But regarding 'Upon a moment of Hades,' the others spoke of a depth. Verse 22.

Signifying many things, as we have said, the principle now denotes the eternal, and the cause, and the productive. And the principle of some things is a principle, and signifies a relation, but not subsistence. For things toward something are such: as the right and the left. Therefore, the Wisdom of God, being a subsistence, is not a principle of any things; for before creation, Wisdom exists. But when it receives a relation toward created things, then it becomes a principle of the productive and providential ways of God, toward the works which have their existence from the Creator, having contributed nothing to it toward being Wisdom; but the relation through which it is called principle and creator, that came to be when the created things came to be. For a principle does not pre-exist those of which it is a principle; nor are these said to exist with it, if the creatures possess their subsistence in time. For Wisdom, being eternal, is not subject to time.

3 Therefore the principle is a spouse to the creatures. The Son of God, pre-existing the creation, being Wisdom, if he says, 'The Lord created me,' he does not have the thought of subsistence, but rather a relation toward the creatures. For he says he is created for works, being the principle of the productive and providential ways of God, that is to say, the cause, to speak more introductory. The Son of God has become man, taking the form of a slave; and being from before the ages and eternal, in that which God is the Word, he is said to be created because he had birth from Mary, becoming flesh; so that those who wish to walk according to God and toward God may use a teacher, providing a pattern of excellent life and instruction to those who follow.

That 'created' does not always signify subsistence, is shown by David saying, 'Create in me a clean heart, O God' (Psalm 51:10). For he asks not as one not possessing, to receive, but as one having cast it away, to receive it again having been cleansed. And Paul, saying the two are created into one new man (Ephesians 2:15), does not signify the subsistence of men, but a union from concord; just as those who interpreted 'He created me' brought it forth. title: Exegesis of Proverbs
english: He stood to him, and he is before all things. And the Lord himself says: 'I am the beginning of the creation of God' (Rev 4:11). For just as a man undergoes becoming, desiring to be a foundation of the Church so that it might be established upon him without being shaken, so also, desiring to provide being to the creation, it has happened according to that, introducing the aforementioned relationship, becoming a beginning and a cause to those who are to come; but even if, he says, it was created according to these things, yet before all things God begets me, which is the Son.

He says that He takes the throne as his own kingdom, and the noetic spirits as winds; or just as David: 'He who walks on the wings of the winds' (Ps 135:6); desiring to present the weaker part of his essence as incorporeal.
See the works being divided: wisdom and God. One was making, he says; but I was joining. And strong, how? We do not need any foundation; for it is held by the will of God alone.

Either that at the same time as appearing he provides life, or that he comes forth to reveal to someone descending toward the weakness of the mind there; for being life, and having come out to those able to see him, he gives life; and he says either will or love, or that he made us autonomous so as to be ready to do what is necessary.
Let him turn away, so that he may receive prudence; for the imperfect is strengthened by the words and mysteries of wisdom.

The same food and meat are named both bread and milk and wine. Moreover, the foolish are said to partake as of their bread and as of poured-out wine; if it is this, how shall we understand? 'A man ate the bread of angels' (Matt 4:4), [meaning] understand for me the solid commands of God as bread, and wine as the knowledge of him from the study of the divine Scriptures; likewise also his divine body and precious blood.

The natural thinker hears, 'The sun shall not burn you by day, nor the moon by night' (Ps 121:6). He calls the worldly cares a burning; and those being dried up by it he calls hay; but the Savior, through the parable, indicates the tribulations; and he called the persecutions according to the word a burning.
The wise man leads the heavy-hearted to perception by a rebuking word. Do you see that it is not to desire that is evil, but to desire such a thing, is evil? Of the
The ungodly have only evil hopes; for everything they hope for is destruction (Proverbs 10:28).

Verse 7. The phrase, “Instead of him,” does not mean as the subject of the pious man is [subjected] to judgment, but because the snare stands from the evil against the righteous; the pious one is rescued from it by God, but the ungodly, having been abandoned by divine providence, falls into it. Or, because the righteous man is subject to certain things as a man is to sins, but the ungodly having come and having done evil to the righteous, has rescued him from sins and from future punishments, while he himself received the punishments; and he is handed over not by anyone else, but by his own wickedness, as having previously handed himself over to an unproven mind.
Verse 4. Those who gather [things] are diminished from virtues; or, those gathering words and not transmitting them.
Verse 10. He who is harsh regarding each of the defects of his own house will be homeless; but a fool will serve a wise man.

Verse 13. An ungodly man, therefore, he says, is one who hates God; but a sinner is one who is evil regarding his actions; and a righteous man here he calls the practical man with word and knowledge; for the precision of righteousness is great.
Verse 6. “The better” is not comparative, but “instead of the good.”
Verse 9. The practical and the private man is more honorable than the one in word and elegant but inactive.
Verse 12. The roots of the righteous will not be uprooted, that is, the good dispositions.

Verse 7. Whatever he says, he says, is confirmed by works; and if it is more certain by work. Or, instead of [saying] “manifestly,” [it is] “established,” “unimpeachable,” to show it sufficiently himself. But a witness of the unrighteous is one who recommends and attempts what he would unrighteously do; and a deceitful man is one who has nothing upright.

Verse 10. The one speaking of punishments disturbs the one currently walking in a practical life; but the one speaking of promises rejoices. For the perfect righteous man will not be afraid from hearing evil, having fear of the Lord who exalts all (Proverbs 10:16).

Verse 16. The righteous, knowing human weakness, forgives, even if the offense is from a friend; or, because recognizing that the friend is according to the image of God, he is in agreement with himself, being moderate, and guarding himself, and having nothing of the enemy's malice, he holds his thoughts stable.
Verse 2. For the one will have the end of virtue, but the others will not have the fruit.
